newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Apr/May fuel oil almost flat.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Apr/May fuel oil almost flat.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps were down at midday on Tuesday on fresh selling pressure with the April/May time spread narrowing to almost flat, traders said.
"Fuel oil is coming off because of the physical offers and high stocks in Singapore," one trader said.
April fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $97.00/$98.50 per tonne, down from Monday's $98.50/99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
May was quoted at $97.00/$98.25 per tonne from Monday's $97.50/$98.50, they said. The April/May spread traded late on Monday at 35 cents per barrel and was bid earlier today at parity.
Traders said the falling prices were due in part to the emergence of fresh offers at lower levels by a local trader who is currently loading a cargo from the Middle East.
The trader sold a 20,000-tonne cargo late on Monday at $101.00 per tonne free-on-board (fob) Singapore, compared to the $102.50 traded on Friday.

Traders said in addition to the offers from the trader, stocks in Singapore are also high due to poor bunker sales as shipowners are taking more volumes from South Korea as prices there are more competitive.
The gas oil swaps slipped slightly on lower overnight crude values where May Brent closed down 40 cents to $19.59 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
April gas oil was last quoted at $26.50/$26.60 down from Monday's $26.90/$27.00 in quiet trading.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) narrowed further on talks of reduced demand from Indonesia and the wide differential between the two products in the physical market.
The physical regrade is currently valued at around minus 1.00 per barrel pushing the forward April regrade to be offered at flat this morning.
